title: Rules that are not per kind
description:
Two sets. The **cross-kind conditionals** hold of a node whatever its kind and cannot sit in one of the eight files without being written eight times; each is carried here as the assertion a composer splices into `allOf`, with the reason beside it and never in place of it. The **cross-node rules** need to see more than one node at once, so no per-file schema can express any of them and a validator over the whole network is the only place they can be decided.

This file also declares `rationale`. It is a profile field the envelope does not carry, and it belongs beside the conditional that requires it rather than in a list of fields nothing in that list explains.

rationale.description: Why the analysis decided this, required wherever `origin` is `modeled`. A reviewer accepts a fact the material stated and disagrees with one the analysis reached, and can do the second only against a reason.

scope_has_no_boundary.why: A scope belongs to no scope. Its absence is what identifies a partition root, so admitting the field on a subdomain would make the root indistinguishable from a node whose parent nobody wrote.

kind_is_the_construct.why: For these four the kind is the construct, so a `ddd` beside it would name the same fact twice — and two homes for one fact is two facts as soon as one is edited.

modeled_needs_rationale.why: A reviewer accepts a fact the material stated and disagrees with one the analysis reached, and can do the second only against a reason. Stated facts owe none: the material is the reason.

authoring_gap_excuses_three.why: An open `kind: authoring` gap is what says the enrichment pass has not run, which is why there is no status field and none to forget. A node claiming to be finished declares the three fields no analysis carries.
authoring_gap_excuses_three.coarse: Any authoring gap excuses all three, rather than each gap excusing the field it names. Unlike the per-kind alternation this one is not narrowed here: the three fields are owed as a set by the pass that writes them, and which of the three a given gap owes is decided by the completeness check, where a per-field answer can be given against the seal.

only_a_context_relates.why: Only a context relates to a context. The field on any other kind names a relationship the context map cannot hold.

x-gap-alternation.why: A node declares everything its kind requires, or declares a gap naming what it lacks. An object incomplete in a way nobody named is indistinguishable from one whose incompleteness is justified.
x-gap-alternation.decided_in: domain/nodes/*.json, one clause per required field
x-gap-alternation.per_field: The clause is written once per field rather than once per kind. A single `anyOf: [ every field, gaps ]` is satisfied by any gap over any field, so a gap about `owner` would excuse a missing `boundary` — and `boundary` is the parent pointer, which is how a node passes validation while hanging off nothing.
x-gap-alternation.not_expressible_here: The converse — that every gap names a fact the kind requires and the node lacks — reads the node's own kind and content together, and is decided by `src/claude/bin/check_knowledge.py` in `problems_for`.
x-gap-alternation.shape_is_load_bearing: `obligations()` in `src/claude/bin/check_knowledge.py` recovers each kind's required-field set by reading this structure out of the composed contract. It accepts both the per-kind form `domain-object/1` carries and the per-field form above; a third shape would make it return an empty set, and the converse check would pass every node while reporting nothing.

identifier_arithmetic.rule: Every identifier computes to the path it sits at, and the kind in the identifier agrees with the kind the node declares.

boundary_agrees_with_identifier.rule: A node's `boundary` names a scope in the same bounded context as its own identifier's scope segment.
boundary_agrees_with_identifier.why: The parent is written twice — once in the identifier, which fixes the path, and once in `boundary`, which fixes membership. The edge table marks `boundary` as `crosses_context: true`, so nothing in the schema stops a node filed under one context from declaring an aggregate in another as its parent, and the two trees then disagree about where the node lives.

gaps_and_absences_agree.rule: Every gap names a fact the kind requires and the node lacks, and every fact it lacks is named by a gap.

lifecycle_totality.rule: For every pairing of a declared state with a trigger the table mentions, either a transition or a rejection exists.

one_lifecycle_per_subject.rule: No two lifecycles name one definition as subject.

root_is_an_aggregate_root.rule: An aggregate's `root` names a definition whose `ddd` is `aggregate-root`, and whose own `boundary` is that aggregate.
root_is_an_aggregate_root.why: "This is the root" is stated twice — by the aggregate's `root` edge and by the definition's `ddd` — and nothing required them to agree. A root sitting outside the aggregate it heads is the same defect from the other side.

containment_is_acyclic.rule: No node reaches itself by following `boundary`, and no context reaches itself by following `subdomain`.
containment_is_acyclic.why: `boundary` admits an aggregate inside an aggregate, so the containment relation is a forest only if nothing closes a loop. A cycle makes the scope of a node undefined and makes the walk that resolves it non-terminating.

crossing_targets_an_interface.rule: A reference whose origin and target sit in different bounded contexts targets an `interface`.

references_resolve.rule: An edge naming an identifier the network does not hold is reported as a defect, never repaired.

x-owed.state_reachability: Every state is reachable from `initial`, and every non-terminal state has an outgoing transition. Specified; no shipped script decides it.
x-owed.cardinality: Every edge's cardinality is enforced. Declared in `tables/edges.json`; only `lifecycle.subject` and `aggregate.root` have their inverse bound decided anywhere, and by hand rather than from the table.
x-owed.orphans: An orphan is reported. The materializer's rule counts a node as referenced when it is the *source* of any edge, and every node but a scope declares a `boundary` — so for six of the eight kinds the rule cannot fire. A semantically isolated node is not the same thing as an orphan, and nothing decides the first.
x-owed.boundary_validation: A node is validated against the frontmatter contract at the boundary. Specified; the distribution ships no validator that does it, and the record and result contracts are checked by model judgment rather than by a script.
x-owed.body_form: One sentence per line, exactly one RFC 2119 keyword, the two headings the kind names, and the body-length ceiling. Specified; nothing decides any of the four.
